sentence: After weeks of deliberation, they finally decided to go ___ with the plan.
explanation: To <go ahead with> significa proceder con algo.
tip: They decided to proceed with the plan.

sentence: The company had to lay ___ a significant portion of its workforce.
explanation: To <lay off> significa despedir empleados, generalmente de forma temporal, debido a condiciones económicas.
tip: The company dismissed a large number of employees.

sentence: He tried to talk her ___ of resigning, but she was determined.
explanation: To <talk someone out of> algo significa persuadir a alguien de que no lo haga.
tip: He tried to persuade her not to resign.

sentence: The new regulations will come ___ effect next month.
explanation: To <come into effect> significa entrar en vigor o volverse válido.
tip: The regulations will become operative next month.

sentence: She always stands ___ for what she believes is right.
explanation: To <stand up for> significa defender o apoyar a alguien o algo.
tip: She defends what she believes is right.

sentence: The project was called ___ at the last minute due to lack of funding.
explanation: To <call off> significa cancelar algo.
tip: The project was cancelled at the last minute.

sentence: He managed to get ___ with only a warning despite breaking the rules.
explanation: To <get away with> significa hacer algo incorrecto o ilegal sin ser castigado o descubierto.
tip: He escaped punishment despite breaking the rules.

sentence: The new manager is trying to crack ___ on absenteeism.
explanation: To <crack down on> significa volverse más estricto al lidiar con algo.
tip: The manager is being stricter about absenteeism.

sentence: I can't quite put my finger ___ what's wrong with this picture.
explanation: To <put your finger on> algo significa identificar con precisión qué está mal o es diferente.
tip: I can't identify precisely what's wrong.

sentence: The company is trying to cut ___ on unnecessary expenses.
explanation: To <cut back on> significa reducir la cantidad de algo.
tip: The company is reducing unnecessary spending.

sentence: He finally came ___ to the idea of moving abroad.
explanation: To <come around to> significa cambiar de opinión o decisión porque alguien te ha persuadido.
tip: He changed his opinion about moving abroad.

sentence: The new policy will bring ___ significant changes to the department.
explanation: To <bring about> significa causar que algo suceda.
tip: The policy will cause significant changes.

sentence: She's always been able to get ___ with people from all walks of life.
explanation: To <get along with> significa tener una relación amistosa con alguien.
tip: She has friendly relationships with all kinds of people.

sentence: The police are looking ___ the cause of the fire.
explanation: To <look into> significa investigar algo.
tip: The police are investigating the cause of the fire.

sentence: The new evidence bears ___ the witness's testimony.
explanation: To <bear out> significa confirmar o respaldar la veracidad de algo.
tip: The evidence confirms the witness's testimony.

sentence: She always puts her ideas ___ clearly and concisely.
explanation: To <put across> significa comunicar una idea o mensaje de manera efectiva.
tip: She communicates her ideas effectively.

sentence: The new policy will take ___ from next Monday.
explanation: To <take effect> significa entrar en vigor.
tip: The policy will become operative on Monday.

sentence: She always stands ___ for her friends when they are in trouble.
explanation: To <stand by> significa apoyar a alguien, especialmente en una situación difícil.
tip: She supports her friends in difficult times.

sentence: She always manages to smooth things ___ when there's a conflict.
explanation: To <smooth over> significa hacer que los problemas o dificultades parezcan menos serios o importantes.
tip: She resolves conflicts — makes problems seem less serious.

sentence: He's been trying to square ___ his actions with his conscience.
explanation: To <square with> significa ser coherente con algo o concordar con ello.
tip: The context tells you whether this is active or passive.

sentence: Years of criticism chipped ___ at his confidence.
explanation: El phrasal verb <chip away> significa debilitar poco a poco.
tip: Partícula de <chip>: debilitar poco a poco

sentence: Investigators zeroed ___ on the suspect's alibi.
explanation: El phrasal verb <zero in> significa concentrarse específicamente en algo.
tip: Partícula de <zero>: concentrarse específicamente en algo

sentence: Researchers tried to tease ___ the underlying causes.
explanation: El phrasal verb <tease out> significa identificar algo complejo con esfuerzo.
tip: Partícula de <tease>: identificar algo complejo con esfuerzo

sentence: She has never shied ___ from controversy.
explanation: El phrasal verb <shy away> significa evitar algo por temor.
tip: Partícula de <shy>: evitar algo por temor

sentence: The new theory builds ___ decades of prior research.
explanation: El phrasal verb <build on> significa basarse en algo existente.
tip: Partícula de <build>: basarse en algo existente

sentence: He tried to pass ___ the copy as an original.
explanation: El phrasal verb <pass off> significa hacer pasar algo por otra cosa.
tip: Partícula de <pass>: hacer pasar algo por otra cosa

sentence: They roped ___ several volunteers for the campaign.
explanation: El phrasal verb <rope in> significa persuadir a alguien para participar.
tip: Partícula de <rope>: persuadir a alguien para participar

sentence: The negotiations wound ___ lasting far longer than expected.
explanation: El phrasal verb <wind up> significa terminar o concluir.
tip: Partícula de <wind>: terminar o concluir

sentence: Negotiators refused to hold ___ any longer.
explanation: El phrasal verb <hold out> significa resistir o aguantar.
tip: Partícula de <hold>: resistir o aguantar

sentence: The committee aims to weed ___ unqualified applicants.
explanation: El phrasal verb <weed out> significa eliminar lo no deseado.
tip: Partícula de <weed>: eliminar lo no deseado
